arguments.arg3: rdx: third argument, passed through to the per-item handler as its fourth argument; its own meaning is not pinned
arguments.db: rsi: pointer to the manager struct (kept as r14)
arguments.out: rdi: pointer to the result struct the function writes and returns (rbx in rax on return)
arguments.returns: the out struct pointer (rdi in rax on return); the struct itself is the result

direct_calls.setup: rdi = rsp + 0x90 (out struct), rsi = rbx (db), rdx = r14 (arg3)

callers.method: byte-pattern scan over the executable segment (file offsets 0x1342c80..0x5660250, vaddr = file offset + 0x1000) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on 0x50ebfb0, plus e9 tail-jump scan and a whole-file qword scan for 0x50ebfb0
callers.note: both call sites decode as call instructions in objdump output; caller purposes are not claimed

collection.list: walk from the head's +0x938 next pointer while the node differs from the head; the node link field is +0x938
collection.order: kept items are appended in walk order
collection.overflow_indexing: for per-item and marking-loop index i >= 8, the item is overflow_begin[i - 8] (the bytes compute overflow_begin - 0x40 + i * 8)
collection.score: otherwise call 0x4feb700(item, overflow-vector slot address); the score's own meaning beyond the threshold comparison is not claimed
collection.skip_flagged: an item whose byte at +0x3d is nonzero is skipped without a score call
collection.storage: the first 8 kept items go to the inline stack array; further items go to the overflow vector, which grows through 0x4fc75e0 when its end equals its capacity
collection.threshold: skip the item when the score is unsigned-below the WAL number; keep it when score >= WAL number
collection.total: total = inline count + (overflow end - overflow begin) / 8

context.base: a stack struct built at -0x140(%rbp) before the loop; phases B/C/D/E/F receive it
context.note: field offsets are relative to the -0x140 base; the 0x100 at +0x50 and 0x00ffffffffffffff at +0x60 are exact initial values
context.teardown_flag: teardown destroys the condition variable at context + 0xc0 only when the byte at context + 0x50 is nonzero; the initial value 0x100 leaves that byte 0, so the destructor runs only if a phase set it

db_fields.field_1698: db+0x1698: the sweep struct passed to the pending-key erase sweep
db_fields.field_360: db+0x360: passed as the logger argument of both log calls
db_fields.field_68_list: db+0x68 points to a struct whose +0x40 field points to a struct whose +0x110 field is the collection list head; list nodes link through +0x938; the head node itself is the sentinel (an empty list has head.next == head)
db_fields.field_700: db+0x700: passed to the entry hook and to phase B
db_fields.field_c28: db+0xc28: the second value of the main log call (the total-log-size slot)
db_fields.field_f50: db+0xf50: passed to phases B and C
db_fields.flag_17b0: db+0x17b0: read at context-init time (nonzero selects phase B before the loop) and in the post-loop chain (nonzero selects phase C)
db_fields.flag_4a3: db+0x4a3: nonzero selects the sweep path at entry
db_fields.flag_4c7: db+0x4c7: read at collection time (nonzero selects phase G instead of collection), per marking-loop item, and in the post-loop chain (nonzero selects phases D+E+F)
db_fields.gate_a_struct: db+0xae0 holds a pointer; that struct's first field (u64) is the WAL number and the collection threshold, and its byte at +0x10 is the gate-A flag
db_fields.not_claimed: no field is given a source-level name; only the offsets and the uses above are pinned

entry_sequence: call 0x5334d60 with (db + 0x700); its own semantics are not claimed
zero the result struct (u32 0, u16 0, pointer 0)
gate A: if the gate-A struct's +0x10 byte is nonzero, return the zeroed result immediately; nothing else is built on this path
gate B: if db+0x4a3 is nonzero, take the sweep path; otherwise take the main path

main_path.collection_gate: if db+0x4c7 is nonzero at collection time, run phase G instead of the collection loop and phase A (see phase_G)
main_path.flag_stores: db+0x1511 is reset to 0 and the gate-A flag byte is set to 1, in that order, before the 0x50e6a90 call

log_call.format: [%s:1638] Flushing all column families with data in WAL number %lu. Total log size is %lu while max_total_wal_size is %lu
slots_in_order: the WAL number (gate-A struct first field)

main_path.third_log_value: 0x50e6a90(db) is called; its return value is the third value of the main log call. Its own semantics beyond that are not claimed

marking_loop.flag_reread: db+0x4c7 is read fresh for each item, so an item whose flag check fails skips only its own per-item phase
marking_loop.gate: runs only when db+0x4c7 is zero, total > 0, and the out low byte is 0, after phase C (when applicable)
marking_loop.per_item: for each collected item in order: set item byte +0x905 to 1; if the s32 at item +0x900 is greater than 0, also set item byte +0x8f0 to 1
marking_loop.per_item_phase: when db+0x4c7 is still zero for that item, additionally run 0x5040500(db, fresh mini context) then 0x503a7f0(db, mini result), free the mini context's 0x18-byte node list, memset its array, reset its counts, and free its overflow buffer when non-null; this per-item phase does NOT call 0x50e89f0 (unlike phase E)

not_claimed: no behavior is claimed for the sibling driver 0x50e8f00..0x50e9402 (a different FDE) beyond phase G's call contract
no behavior is claimed for the handler's work on any single item beyond the result copy

the 0x50ec810 phase-B path's total==0 branch that would re-check db+0x17b0 is unreachable on that path (phase B is entered only when db+0x17b0 is nonzero); it is recorded as observed control flow, not as a live arm

per_item_loop.bounds: index i runs from 0 while i != total; the loop head re-reads the total from the saved slot, and the body re-checks the stop byte before each item
per_item_loop.completion: when i reaches total with the out low byte still 0, control goes to the post-loop chain's completion entry
per_item_loop.early_exit: when the result copy leaves the out low byte nonzero, the loop ends immediately (remaining items are not processed) and control goes to the post-loop chain's early-exit entry
per_item_loop.handler_call: 0x50ea260(result struct, db, item, arg3, context); call site 0x50ec2d1; the handler's internals are NOT pinned — only its result-struct contract (see result_struct) is
per_item_loop.item_fetch: i < 8 reads the inline array slot i; i >= 8 reads overflow_begin[i - 8]
per_item_loop.refcount: item + 0x38 is incremented with a locked add before the handler call
per_item_loop.release: 0x4ff0bb0(item) is called after the copy; its internals are not pinned
per_item_loop.result_copy: out+0 = result u32; out+4 = result u16 (result u16 then zeroed); out+8 = result pointer (previous out pointer freed with sized operator delete when non-null)

phase_A.note: runs after collection on the main path only; its internals are not pinned

phase_B.note: runs before the per-item loop only when db+0x17b0 is nonzero at context-init time; its internals are not pinned

phase_G.note: runs instead of collection and phase A when db+0x4c7 is nonzero at collection time; after it, control jumps to the context init with an empty collection (total 0). Its internals are not pinned

post_loop.flag_4c7_chain: when the out low byte is 0: if db+0x4c7 is nonzero, run phase D, then phase E, then phase F, then teardown; if db+0x4c7 is zero, run the marking loop when total > 0 (or skip it when total == 0), then phase E, then phase F, then teardown
post_loop.out_recheck: after phase C (and on the early-exit entry when phase C is skipped), a nonzero out low byte goes straight to teardown, skipping phases D, E, F and the marking loop

phase_C.gate: runs only when db+0x17b0 is nonzero, on both the early-exit and the completion entries; its internals are not pinned

phase_E.context_fields: the phase-E context carries 1 at its +0x08 slot (0x250 offset in the stack frame), 0 at +0x10 and +0x18, and 1.0 as a float at +0x20
phase_E.note: phase-E internals are not pinned beyond the call order

result_struct.entry: all three fields are zeroed at entry (after the entry hook call)
result_struct.handler_copy: after each handler call, out+0 takes the handler result's u32, out+4 takes its u16 (and the handler result's u16 field is then zeroed), out+8 takes its pointer (and the previous out pointer, when non-null, is freed with sized operator delete)
result_struct.layout: u32 at +0, u16 at +4, heap pointer at +8
result_struct.not_claimed: the struct is NOT identified as any named library type; only its three fields and the copy/stop rules above are pinned
result_struct.stop_rule: the per-item loop and the post-loop phase chain continue only while the low byte of the +0 field is 0; a nonzero low byte stops the loop and skips the remaining phases

sweep_path.call: 0x5160560 (the pending-key erase sweep mapped in #1798) with (db + 0x1698); this is the sweep's site-3 caller at 0x50ec61e
sweep_path.note: gate A is checked only once, at entry; neither the re-enter nor the restart path re-checks it
sweep_path.result_equal_flag_clear: if the sweep returns exactly the WAL number and db+0x1511 is 0, log once at level 2 (file db/db_impl/db_impl_write.cc, message '[%s:1621] Unable to release oldest log due to uncommitted transaction', no value slots), set db+0x1511 to 1, and restart the main body WITHOUT resetting db+0x1511 and WITHOUT setting the gate-A flag (the restart jumps to the 0x50e6a90 call, past both stores)
sweep_path.result_equal_flag_set: if the sweep returns exactly the WAL number and db+0x1511 is already nonzero, return the current result immediately; the main body does not run
sweep_path.result_zero_or_other: if the sweep returns 0, or a value different from the WAL number, re-enter the main path at its entry (reset db+0x1511 to 0, set the gate-A flag byte to 1, then run the main body)

teardown.buffers: free the context's heap buffers with sized operator delete when non-null
teardown.canary: the stack canary is checked; failure calls __stack_chk_fail
teardown.collection_reset: reset the inline count to 0 and free the overflow vector buffer when non-null (end reset to begin first)
teardown.condition_variable: destroy the condition variable at context + 0xc0 only when the byte at context + 0x50 is nonzero

unknowns: the 0x50e6a90 return value's own meaning beyond being the third main-log value
the 0x4feb700 score's own meaning beyond the threshold comparison
the per-item handler 0x50ea260's internals beyond its result-struct contract
the internals of phases A, B, C, D, E, F, G
the source-level names of every db field (only offsets and uses are pinned)
the roles of the context fields beyond their initial values and the teardown flag

window.frame: pushes r15/r14/r13/r12/rbp/rbx, 0x268-byte stack adjustment, canary fs:0x28 at rsp-0x38, checked on every return path
window.note: single FDE; the tail stubs at 0x50ec983..0x50ec9d7 are exception landing pads that jump back into the function body. The next FDE starts at 0x50ec9d7.
